Closing entries and trial balance

Closes the year's income and expenses into owners' equity, tests that the platform has not closed it already, and proves the post-closing trial balance.

Watch someone use it

Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, a two-member LLC, closing the year ended 31 December 2025. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

Claudewith the MosoFin closing entries and trial balance skill

Can you close our books for 2025?

Claude

Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.

  1. Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
  2. Which company? For a group, which entities?
  3. When does your fiscal year end?
  4. Is the business a corporation, partnership, LLC, sole proprietor or nonprofit?
  5. For a partnership or LLC: how do the members share profit, and do you keep capital for each member?
  6. Which framework: US GAAP, IFRS or other?
  7. Is this the final trial balance, with all adjusting entries posted?
  8. Does your accounting system close the year by itself when you move to the new year?
  9. Is the audit complete?
  10. Do you close straight to retained earnings, or through an Income Summary account?
  11. Do you report on a cash or an accrual basis?

Use MosoFin. Northbrook Trading. It is an LLC. Lena Hart gets 60% and Omar Vance 40%, with capital kept for each. US GAAP, accrual. We have no Income Summary account. All adjustments are in. I think QuickBooks closes the year. The audit is not done. Last year's K-1s are attached.

📄 2024-schedule-k1s.pdf
MosoFinChecked the workspace and the company fileread-only✓
  1. WorkspaceNorthbrook Trading
  2. Company fileQuickBooks Online, confirmed by name
  3. get_company_infoYear-end 31 December, US dollars
  4. Account typesEnabled
  5. ToolsRead-only tools only

The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

Claude

Here is my plan. I close FY2025, the year ended 31 December 2025, for Northbrook Trading, an LLC with capital for each member. I use the two-step method, straight to capital, because you have no Income Summary account. The audit is not complete, so this is a preliminary close. Before I propose any entry, I test whether QuickBooks already closed the year. Shall I start?

Yes, go ahead.

MosoFinRead the books in one batchread-only✓
  1. search_accounts24 accounts, includes Customer Deposits as Other Income
  2. get_trial_balanceRead
  3. get_profit_and_lossNet income 212,900
  4. get_balance_sheetRead
  5. get_general_ledgerRead
  6. search_journal_entriesRead

6 reads in one batch. Nothing in your books changed.

Claude

Before I go on, one account needs your answer. Customer Deposits has the type Other Income and a credit of $4,000. The name says money that customers paid in advance. That is a liability, not income. If the name is right, this correction is needed first:

Correction for you to post
AccountAmountSide
Customer Deposits, income account$4,000Debit
Customer Deposits, liability account$4,000Credit

Net income agrees with the P&L at 212,900, because the P&L follows the same type. So only a check of names against types finds this. Which is right, the name or the type? If it is the name, the trial balance is not final. Please post the correction in QuickBooks, dated 31 December 2025, and tell me. Net income then falls to $208,900.

The name. Customers paid that money in advance. I posted the correction. Please run it again.

MosoFinRead the books again, and tested the closed stateread-only✓
  1. get_trial_balance31 Dec 2025, 1,724,000 on each side
  2. get_trial_balance1 Jan 2026, every income and expense account at 0
  3. search_journal_entriesNo closing entry near 31 Dec 2025
  4. get_balance_sheetRetained Earnings 208,900 at 1 Jan 2026
  5. get_profit_and_lossNet income 208,900
  6. get_general_ledgerMember capital and distributions

6 reads in one batch. Nothing in your books changed.

Claude

You were right. QuickBooks already closed the year. On 1 January 2026, every income and expense account is at 0. No closing entry exists, and Retained Earnings holds the year's $208,900.

So I propose no entry that closes revenue or expenses. A second close would count the profit twice and overstate equity by $208,900. The final trial balance balances at 1,724,000 on each side. Opening capital of $350,000 agrees with the ending capital on your 2024 K-1s.

Claude

QuickBooks moved the profit into Retained Earnings. It did not split it between the members, and it did not close their distributions. I propose two entries for that:

Proposed entries, 31 Dec 2025
EntryAmountDebit and credit
P1, Lena Hart's 60% of $208,900$125,340Dr Retained Earnings, Cr Member Capital (Hart)
P1, Omar Vance's 40% of $208,900$83,560Dr Retained Earnings, Cr Member Capital (Vance)
P2, close Lena's distributions$60,000Dr Member Capital (Hart), Cr Member Distributions (Hart)
P2, close Omar's distributions$40,000Dr Member Capital (Vance), Cr Member Distributions (Vance)

Each account has its own name from your chart. A person posts these entries. I do not.

Claude

After P1 and P2, the members' capital moves by exactly the profit and the distributions:

Members' capital, FY2025
Opening capital$350,000
+ Net income, P1$208,900
− Distributions, P2$100,000
= Closing capital$458,900
Lena Hart $275,340 and Omar Vance $183,560$458,900

The post-closing trial balance balances at 591,400 on each side. It holds only permanent accounts. Assets and liabilities did not change.

Claude

This is a preliminary close. If the audit changes any figure, I run the tests again. Your workpaper has eight sheets, with the closed-state finding in its header.

Claude

Here is Closing_Entries_TB_FY2025_Northbrook Trading.xlsx. I cannot post anything. A person posts P1 and P2 in QuickBooks. The coverage sheet names the lock as a manual step for Lena Hart, after the audit.

Do you want me to save your settings for next year?

Yes, save them.

Claude

Done. I saved the entity type, the profit shares, the equity accounts and the two-step method. I also saved that QuickBooks closes the year, the Customer Deposits exception and who locks the period. I never save balances. Next year, I test the closed state again.
